expectations.text: finds-per-grant-hget-loop-453: a finding names the per-grant HGET loop at or around line 453 and proposes batching it (HMGET)

Line 453 — HGET KEYS[7] once per old grant field (highest impact)' quotes the call and proposes 'one chunked_call('HMGET', KEYS[7], old_grant_fields)', '8192 calls -> 32 calls at the current chunk size, 9 at 1000'. expectations.text: addresses-multikey-coordination-cost: the review addresses the coordination cost of this 14-key script on default flags (io vs shard-local) and the --lock_on_hashtags trade-off
expectations.evidence: REVIEW.md:8-17 'A shared hashtag does not co-locate keys on one shard on default flags. It is a lock/placement unit only under --lock_on_hashtags ... io-coordinated regime (a) ... 26.95 µs/call ... versus 1.01 µs on the shard-local path [lab Q5]'. The trade-off is worked through at REVIEW.md:276-281: lock_on_hashtags 'would move this script to ~1.5 µs/call' but 'serialises all unrelated work behind {inbound}'s shard', with the distinct-tags>=shard-count rule and 'Batching ... is the change that pays in both regimes; do this before touching flags.'

expectations.text: claims-carry-dragonfly-evidence: every performance claim names Dragonfly-specific evidence (a measurement run, INFO/eval coordination counters, SCRIPT LATENCY, or a Dragonfly v1.34.0 doc/source citation)
expectations.evidence: Each cost claim is tied to a cited measurement: 26.95 vs 1.01 µs/call [lab Q5] (:13-14), HGET->HMGET p50 41183->7814 µs, p99 52222->17150 µs [lab Q7] and 7.6x [lab Q10] (:47-48), plan encode p50 1905 µs at 1 MiB / 15070 µs at 8 MiB and the 32 MiB OOM [lab Q4] (:114-116), replica write cost +4.3%/+41.6% [lab Q6] (:138-139), acall 28.05->2.93 µs/call [lab Q5] (:192), unpack limit 8163 [lab Q9] (:216). Verification names eval_io_coordination_total vs eval_shardlocal_coordination_total (:252), total_commands_processed deltas (:256) and scripts/script_latency.py (:273).

expectations.text: no-unverified-redis-only-advice: no Redis Functions/FUNCTION migration, no '#!lua flags=no-writes' shebang, no disable-atomicity-for-speed, no client pipelining as the fix for in-script calls, no redis.setresp(3) -- unless backed by Dragonfly evidence
expectations.evidence: No FUNCTION, no setresp, no pipelining-as-fix anywhere. Shebang-style directives appear only as an explicit warning backed by evidence: REVIEW.md:201-202 'Do not reach for --lua_auto_async here ... the --!df flags= directives are not an optimisation — both real flags remove the fast path, and no-writes is parsed and ignored [lab Q5]'. The atomicity-relevant suggestion (redis.acall for discarded replies, :188-199) is Dragonfly-specific and measured, and it explicitly requires verifying ordering barriers and error surfacing.

expectations.text: flags-redundant-writes: the review flags as redundant writes both the delete-and-reinsert of unchanged grants at apply_new_mutable_mailbox_page.lua:612-616 (HDEL/ZREM of grant fields followed by HSET/ZADD of the same rows) and the rewrite at apply_new_mutable_mailbox_page.lua:403-415 of records and grants the script has already compared and proven identical, and states that these writes still cost shard mutations, journal bytes and replica bytes
expectations.evidence: REVIEW.md:135-150 '## 4. Lines 403-415 and 612-616 — writes the script has already proven redundant' covers both: ':403-409 existing_records proves every already-present record_field is byte-identical ...
